evals.prompt: Create a Go service with a POST /orders endpoint that places an order with lines and returns the total. Use the standard library router and PostgreSQL with pgx.
evals.setup: Empty directory with go.mod (module shop, go 1.26).
expectations: Packages are organized by bounded context under internal/, then domain / app / adapters (inbound, outbound)
No package under domain/ or app/ imports net/http, pgx, database/sql or a web framework
Money is int64 minor units, never float64; ids are defined types
Ports are interfaces declared in the app package; use cases receive them through a NewX constructor
Domain structs have unexported fields and no json or db tags
Errors are sentinels wrapped with %w and mapped to application/problem+json in one place
context.Context is the first parameter of every method that does I/O
main.go sets server timeouts and shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM
A use case test uses in-memory fakes and no database
A depguard configuration (or an equivalent architecture check) is included
The answer reports which checks were run (gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint, go test -race) and their result, or says they were not run

evals.prompt: Refactor this Gin handler into a use case with a repository port. Keep the HTTP behavior identical.
evals.setup: A Gin app whose POST /orders handler binds JSON, runs SQL with a *sql.DB global, computes the total and writes c.JSON with ad hoc error bodies, all in one function.
expectations: Characterization tests of the current HTTP behavior (httptest) come first, or are explicitly proposed before the change
The handler becomes thin: bind, call the use case, render; errors go through c.Error and one middleware
SQL moves into an outbound adapter behind a repository interface declared by the app package
The global *sql.DB is replaced by explicit wiring in main
Status codes and response bodies of the endpoint are unchanged

evals.prompt: Review this service for architecture problems.
evals.setup: An Echo project whose domain Order struct has gorm and json tags, whose services take echo.Context, and which returns echo.NewHTTPError from the service layer.
expectations: Findings are ordered by severity and use the format [severity] path:line — rule — consequence — fix
The GORM model used as domain entity is reported as a blocker
echo.Context and echo.NewHTTPError outside the adapter are reported
Fixes are the smallest local change, not a rewrite

evals.prompt: Add CRUD endpoints for product categories (name and slug, nothing else).
evals.setup: An existing hexagonal Go project with net/http and pgx.
expectations: The answer uses a thin slice: one package with the record, a port and the use cases; no aggregate, no events, no outbox
A port still separates the use cases from SQL
Uniqueness relies on a unique constraint translated to a conflict error, not only on a check-then-insert
The existing layout and naming of the project are followed

evals.prompt: Add an endpoint to our Fiber API that cancels an order by id and publishes an OrderCancelled event.
evals.setup: A Fiber v3 project with the base hexagonal layout and the default fiber.Config.
expectations: The answer sets Immutable: true or copies values taken from fiber.Ctx before they reach the use case
fiber.Ctx is not passed to the application layer; c.Context() is
The event goes to an outbox in the same transaction as the order update, not straight to a broker
A stale version or a forbidden transition maps to 409 through the central error handler
